response:
Austin and Raleigh offer a fairly similar economic profile, but they differ notably in scale, housing costs, and climate. Austin is much larger—about 1.0 million residents in 2025 versus roughly 506,000 in Raleigh. Raleigh, however, grew faster since 2020: 8.6% compared with Austin’s 4.2%, so it has been the faster-growing city proportionally.

The clearest practical tradeoff is housing. In 2024, Austin’s median rent was $1,729 and its median home value was $555,300, compared with $1,572 and $415,800 in Raleigh. Austin also had the higher median household income, $93,658 versus $85,395. In other words, Austin combines higher reported incomes with noticeably higher housing costs; Raleigh is less expensive on both rent and home values, though its income level is lower as well. Raleigh also had a larger owner share—50.7% versus Austin’s 43.4%—while Austin’s households were more likely to rent.

Climate is another substantial difference. The 1991–2020 normals show Austin with much warmer winters and hotter summers: January’s normal mean is 52.2°F in Austin versus 41.7°F in Raleigh, while August averages 86.5°F versus 78.7°F. Raleigh is generally wetter in many of the warmer months, especially June through September. Snowfall values are not supplied for either city, so the comparison can establish the temperature and precipitation differences but not make a snowfall comparison.

Both cities have highly educated populations and similar commute times. The share of adults with a bachelor’s degree or higher was 59.6% in Austin and 54.0% in Raleigh, while average commute times were close—23.7 minutes and 23.0 minutes, respectively. Austin had a higher work-from-home share, 30.7% versus 25.8%. Neither city’s reported commute pattern suggests that transit is a dominant mode: transit shares were 2.0% in Austin and 1.4% in Raleigh.

Reported 2024 violent-crime rates were broadly similar—466.9 per 100,000 in Austin and 488.8 in Raleigh—so the difference is not large enough to treat as a decisive distinction here. Austin’s reported property-crime rate was higher, at 3,241.9 versus 2,819.2 per 100,000. Those figures come from city-level FBI reporting populations and should be read as descriptive comparisons rather than a complete measure of everyday safety.

Overall, Austin is the larger, hotter, more expensive city, with higher income, more bachelor’s-degree attainment, and more work from home. Raleigh is smaller but growing faster, with cooler and generally wetter conditions and lower housing costs. The stronger fit depends on whether you place more weight on Austin’s scale and warmer climate or Raleigh’s lower housing costs and milder summer temperatures.
